implementation_notes: Protobuf's schema is the published language and gRPC C++ supplies the transport and generated abstract service; the host implements one class per service, mapping generated messages to domain operations. Choose it when consumers are remote or written in other languages, and treat the .proto as the artifact consumers bind to.
pitfalls: Generated message classes make it tempting to pass domain data through unchanged, but renaming or removing a field breaks every generated client at once.
Blocking work inside a gRPC handler occupies a thread from the server's pool; keep heavy domain calls bounded or off the completion queue.

variants.name: Published header + pimpl with symbol-versioned shared library
variants.implementation_notes: For consumers that link the subsystem rather than call it, the protocol is the public header: an abstract interface returned by a factory, a pimpl that keeps every member out of the header, and a linker version script that exports only the published symbols under stable versions. This is how long-lived C++ libraries (Boost, Qt, libstdc++) let old binaries keep binding to old symbols while internals are refactored.
pitfalls: pimpl hides the layout, not the ABI: virtual-function order and symbol versions still freeze once published, so a version script is mandatory.
Inline and template functions are compiled into consumers, freezing the implementation copied there; keep them out of the public header or re-release with a new version.
